description: The plain-JSON requirement form of 2026-07, migrated into the requirement management section; records in this form are carried into signed requirement cells (561-group.requirement.v1) by group-requirements convert.
$comment: What a requirement's spec must carry: who asked, what they asked for in their own words, and the conditions under which they would agree it was met. A specific requirement — emsenn/requirement/offices-render-as-a-dag — is its own schema, and this says what any such schema must look like. A requirement is NOT a work item: a requirement is what a party outside the work asked for, and a work item is an act framed with assignment, lifecycle, and a settling target. One requirement is realized by zero or more work items and is met when its own conditions settle, which is a different question from whether the work items finished.

id.$comment: The spec's address. A requirement resolves by it, and the address says emsenn/requirement — a requirement is not a term, it is a thing the term 'requirement' specifies.

name.$comment: What the requirement is called, as it is said.

raised-by.$comment: The party who asked, and who holds the claim that it is met. A requirement nobody raised is not a requirement, it is an idea the firm had about itself. Under 用户付薪 this party is ultimately the end user, and during bootstrap it is usually emsenn; the field exists so the difference is visible rather than assumed.

asks.$comment: What was asked, in the raiser's own words rather than in the firm's. Kept unedited on purpose: the moment this is rewritten into the firm's vocabulary, the record stops being able to show that what was built is not what was asked for.

met-when.$comment: The conditions under which the raiser would agree this was met, as commands a machine runs. minItems 1 because a requirement with no conditions cannot fail, and a requirement that cannot fail is one every output satisfies. This is the whole refusal: prose here means the raiser is the acceptance test, and a raiser who must be consulted to grade the work has not been relieved of anything.

tier.$comment: Which body decides it: routine at the requirements analysis team, major at the requirements management team, strategic at the integrated portfolio management team. Recorded rather than derived because it is a judgement, and recorded BECAUSE it is a judgement — an unrecorded tier is a decision that happened with nothing showing who made it or that it was made at all.

realized-by.$comment: The work items realizing it. Zero is a real state and means distributed to nobody. This is not a claim that the requirement is met: work items finishing and a requirement being met are different questions, and conflating them is how a firm ships a perfectly discharged obligation the user did not want.

changes.$comment: The requirement this one changes. A change to an accepted requirement is a new requirement decided by the requirements management team, never an edit to the old one: editing it in place destroys the evidence that what was asked for moved.

from-idea.$comment: The idea this requirement formalizes, when it formalizes one. Optional and additive. The trace that lets an idea's openness be derived rather than asserted, per the change-control board's ruling at emsenn/decision-record/ideas-dispose-through-the-requirement-term: an idea is open until some requirement names it here, or a decision record names it directly.

$comment-absences: No state, no status, no closed, no verified, no met: whether a requirement is met is READ by re-running met-when, and a spec that could assert it would assert a readout — which is the Work Method's violation and the exact failure mode that makes a worker's report of its own success indistinguishable from evidence. No analysed-by, decided-by, distributed-by, or verified-by: who acted is the offices' business and belongs to the acts, not to the artifact they acted on; a requirement naming the office that analysed it would let the requirement, rather than the roster, say who holds what. No priority: priority without a decider is a feeling, and with one it is the tier.

command.$comment: The command that settles the cell. Its exit code is the settlement: 0 is held, non-zero is denied. A condition with no command is prose wearing a schema's clothes.
